forensics.prep_decoded: decoded the {ctype} part from base64 ({size} B)
forensics.prep_truncated: source truncated to {n} characters (limit for sending to the LLM)
forensics.sender.message_flag: message flag set by the sender (Outlook shows it next to the message) - an attention-grabbing technique
forensics.sender.importance: importance declared by the sender (affects only the display in the client)
forensics.sender.x_priority: priority declared by the sender (1 = highest)
forensics.sender.return_receipt: delivery receipt request (tracking: confirms that the mailbox is alive)
forensics.sender.read_receipt: read receipt request (tracking: confirms that the message was opened)
forensics.flag.scl: Recipient filter (Microsoft): SCL={scl} (0-1 clean, 5-6 spam, 9 highest spam confidence).
forensics.flag.junk: The message was delivered to the Junk folder (RF:JunkEmail / dest:J markers in the filter delivery header).
forensics.flag.anonymous: The message entered the tenant anonymously (AuthAs: Anonymous), without an authenticated sender identity.
forensics.flag.spam_flag: The recipient's anti-spam filter marked the message as spam (X-Spam-Flag: YES).
forensics.flag.high_priority: The sender declares high priority (`{header}: {value}`) - an element of pressure.
forensics.flag.bad_cte: Invalid Content-Transfer-Encoding: `{cte}` (part {ctype}) - the filter and the client may interpret it differently (parser differential).
forensics.flag.boundary_digits: Boundary `{boundary}` contains a hand-typed digit sequence (imitates a generator).
forensics.flag.digest: `multipart/digest` is meant for bundles of messages (message/rfc822) but contains text/HTML parts - unusual, it makes parsing harder.
forensics.flag.duplicate: Header `{name}` appears {n} times (it should appear once)
forensics.flag.non_ascii: Non-ASCII characters in headers without RFC 2047 encoding: {headers} (an export/paste may have caused it).
forensics.hop.id_params: the id field contains URL parameters (`{id}`)
forensics.hop.same_time_as_date: the time of the oldest Received is identical to Date down to the second
forensics.role.oldest_operator: the oldest entry of the recipient's operator - the first record of the connection, IP from the TCP socket (trust boundary)
forensics.role.internal_hop: internal hop of the same operator (after the trust boundary)
forensics.trust_note: The whole Received chain belongs to one operator ({operator}) - it is the recipient's infrastructure. The trust boundary is the oldest entry (#{index}): it recorded the IP address of the connection; the higher entries are internal hops of the same operator.
forensics.role.top: the top one - added by the recipient's server (trust boundary)
forensics.role.below: below the trust boundary - unverified unless its author is trusted
forensics.role.walked_boundary: trust boundary - here the external operator recorded the address of the actually connecting client; the entries above are its own internal network forwarding the message onward
forensics.walked_warning: Be careful: the sender address was taken from older Received lines written by an external relay, not by the recipient's own server, and a sender can forge such lines. The recipient's server recorded the connection from {ip} (the relay).
forensics.flag.domainkey: The `DomainKey-Signature` header is present (an obsolete predecessor of DKIM).
forensics.flag.reply_to: Reply-To is in a different domain than From (a classic warning sign).
forensics.flag.punycode: The domain `{domain}` uses punycode/non-ASCII characters (a possible homoglyph).
forensics.flag.delay: {h} h {m} min passed between `Date` and the top Received (a large delay).
forensics.flag.future_date: `Date` is later than the time of the top Received (a date from the future relative to delivery).
forensics.flag.no_plain: There is no `text/plain` part (HTML only) - legitimate bulk mailings usually add a text alternative.
forensics.flag.big_comment: Large HTML comments ({chars} characters in {count} comments) - possible filler (Bayesian poisoning).
forensics.flag.unknown_tags: {n} unknown HTML tags (possible hash busting), e.g. {list}.
forensics.flag.wrapped_anchor: A large part of the content is wrapped in a single link (style `display:block`): every click leads to the target page.
forensics.flag.tracking: {n} images look like tracking pixels (1x1 or with parameters in the URL).
forensics.flag.link_mismatch: Link: the visible text points to a different domain than the href (`{text}` -> `{host}`).
forensics.flag.link_abused: A link to a service often abused to host phishing: `{host}`.
forensics.flag.link_shortener: A link through a URL shortener: `{host}`.
forensics.flag.link_params: A link with many URL parameters (tracking identifiers?).
forensics.flag.x_originating: The `X-Originating-IP` header may be an infrastructure leak or a decoy - it is not suitable for reports without confirmation in a trusted Received.
forensics.flag.below_received: Headers with names used by the recipient/provider are BELOW all the Received headers (text written by the sender, not by the server): {list}.
error.cross_site_blocked: request from another web page blocked
urlscan.url_too_long: the URL is too long (the limit is {limit} characters)
urlscan.url_whitespace: the URL contains spaces or control characters
urlscan.url_scheme: only http:// and https:// addresses can be scanned (got "{scheme}")
urlscan.url_invalid: this is not a valid URL
urlscan.url_private: urlscan.io scans only public internet hosts; "{host}" is a local or private address
urlscan.invalid_useragent: invalid user agent (up to 250 printable characters)
report.hard_checks_failed: the hard checks did not pass
report.cooldown: this IP was reported less than {limit} minutes ago - AbuseIPDB accepts the next report of the same IP only after {limit} minutes ({minutes} min left)
report.age_future: the attack date is in the future
report.duplicate_remote: AbuseIPDB refused the report: the same IP can be reported by one account only once in {limit} minutes (the report may have been sent from elsewhere)
report.daily_limit: the AbuseIPDB daily report limit ({limit}) is used up - reports are accepted again from {when}
report.key_rejected: AbuseIPDB rejected the API key (missing, wrong or without the right to report) - check ABUSEIPDB_API_KEY in .env
lookup.invalid_indicator: not a valid IP address or domain name: {indicator}
parser.relay_note: The first hop outside the recipient's domain is the operator relay '{relay}', not the sender, so I walked further along the chain ({chain}) to the hop where the operator recorded the address of the actually connecting sender.
parser.relay_walk_warning: Be careful: this address is less certain. It comes from older Received lines written by the relay itself, not by your own mail server, and a sender can forge such lines. Your server recorded the connection from {ip} (the relay). Check the address before you report it.
parser.relay_declined: Note: older Received lines written by '{relay}' exist below this hop, but '{relay}' is not a known mail provider, so they were not used (a sender could have forged them). They are still listed in the route if you want to look at them.
parser.no_received: There are no Received headers in the e-mail.
parser.origin_inside_provider: The message originated inside a shared mail provider (e.g. webmail or a Microsoft/Google account) - the Received chain contains no public IP address of the sender, only addresses of the provider's relays, which must not be reported to AbuseIPDB. Report the abuse to the provider's abuse department.
parser.no_ip: Could not extract an IP address from any Received header - verify manually.
parser.boundary: Boundary hop: 'from {host}' no longer belongs to the trusted domain '{domain}' (determined from the 'by' header of the newest hop) - it is the first place in the chain where the recipient's own infrastructure records the address of the actually connecting sender.
parser.single_received: A single Received header without a recognisable 'by' domain - its IP was taken as is.
parser.whole_chain_trusted: The whole Received chain stays in the domain '{domain}' - no unambiguous boundary of the trusted infrastructure was found, the oldest hop was taken as the most likely one. Verify manually.
parser.no_public_ip: no reliable public IP found in the Received chain
parser.smtp_auth_consistent: An Authentication-Results header immediately adjacent to this hop (original header order, not a text match) confirms an authenticated SMTP-AUTH account '{account}', whose domain matches the validated DKIM domain '{domain}' - an extra signal that this is not a shared or spoofed relay.
parser.smtp_auth_mismatch: Note: the SMTP-AUTH account '{account}' from the adjacent Authentication-Results header has a different domain than the validated DKIM '{domain}' - treat this corroboration with caution.
parser.smtp_auth_no_dkim: An adjacent Authentication-Results header confirms an authenticated SMTP-AUTH account '{account}', but there is no DKIM domain to cross-check it against (no header.d=).
score.greynoise_no_data: greynoise: no data (neutral - does not affect the score)
score.otx_validated: OTX: IP marked as validated/false positive
score.cloudflare_excluded: cloudflare_radar (network/context data, not a verdict - outside the numeric score)
score.note_contradiction: Contradicting signals: {reasons} - but {sources} indicates high risk. The score is not lowered.
score.note_low_confidence: Low confidence: the score is based on {basis}.
md.status.not_applicable: not applicable to this type of indicator
md.score_based_on: The score is based on {used} of {possible} sources.
us.title: Scan result
us.http_status: HTTP status of the main page
us.cert_age: Certificate age on the day of the scan (days)
us.form_signal: A password form posts to another domain or over plain HTTP - a typical phishing kit
svc.not_applicable: the service does not support this type of indicator
svc.greynoise_community: community (the key has no access to the full IP Lookup /v3/ip)
svc.greynoise_limit: GreyNoise search limit of your plan is used up - the answer will be available again after the limit resets.
svc.greynoise_limit_reset: GreyNoise search limit of your plan is used up - it resets on {date}. The score is computed without this source.
cite.ip_missing: the IP address does not appear in the source or in the deterministic analysis
cite.header_missing: the header "{name}" is not in the source (it may be an example from a legitimate message)
cite.header_mismatch: the quoted header fragment does not match the source
cite.value_differs: the header is in the source, but the quoted value differs
cite.number_missing: such a value does not appear in the source or in the deterministic analysis
cite.identifier_missing: the identifier/digest does not appear in the source or in the deterministic analysis
or.hint.402: insufficient OpenRouter credits or the credit limit was exceeded
or.hint.403: access denied (content moderation or missing key permissions)
or.hint.502: the model or provider is unavailable
or.hint.503: no provider available for the model
or.refusal: the model refused to analyse this message (its safety filter blocked the answer, finish_reason={reason}). This is not a Seisa error and retrying does not help - try another model in OPENROUTER_MODEL
email.source_too_large: The source is too large ({size} characters, limit {limit}).
history.too_large: the history entry data is too large
history.invalid_data: the history entry data is incomplete
history.invalid_thumbnail: the thumbnail must be a JPEG image of a limited size
identity.title: Address identity
identity.note_reg_loc: The registration country ({registration}) differs from the geolocation country ({location}) - usually normal (hosting, anycast, leased ranges).
lookup.non_public_ip: {indicator} is not a public IP address (private, loopback, reserved or documentation range) - the reputation services know nothing about it
heur.homograph: look-alike characters from mixed alphabets in the name ({decoded})
identity.note_nxdomain: The domain does not exist in DNS (NXDOMAIN) - it is unregistered, expired or taken down.
identity.note_wildcard: The zone answers for any subdomain (wildcard DNS) - a random name resolves too; common for parked domains and for phishing kits.
identity.note_ns_missing: The zone is delegated to name servers that do not exist in DNS: {hosts}. The zone cannot be fully resolved, and whoever registers such a name can take the zone over (a dangling NS).
icon.comment: Local tool for checking IP addresses, URLs, DMARC reports and e-mails
icon.unsupported_os: an application icon is supported on macOS and Linux only
icon.no_display: no graphical session found (DISPLAY / WAYLAND_DISPLAY is not set), so there is no menu to put an icon in
icon.no_tools: the macOS tools sips and iconutil are missing, so the icon cannot be made
icon.files_missing: seisa-launcher.sh or frontend/logo.png is missing from the Seisa folder
icon.bad_path: the Seisa folder path contains a control character, an icon cannot be made for it
icon.foreign: {path} already exists and was not made by Seisa, so it was left untouched
icon.build_failed: making the icon failed ({tool} returned an error)
